prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1364; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the insured's representative, who reported a side impact at a signalized intersection and a back strain to the claimant, who was the driver of the vehicle struck on the passenger side.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss, with nothing suggesting the damage happened before coverage started.

Entry 3: Police report and two statements confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact, though no independent witness has come forward to describe the collision itself and no photographs of the scene have been provided.

Entry 4: Reviewed the vehicle file and found no earlier damage recorded on the vehicle, but the repair estimate covers more panels than the impact area clearly shows, so it is not yet clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.

Entry 5: Claimant's representative provided medical records showing a back strain treated with physiotherapy and medication; the reported injury is plausible for a crash of this type, and no earlier injury to the same body area appears in the records we hold.

Entry 6: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so I have asked the treating provider for a note explaining the continued care before setting any reserve.

Entry 7: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far, including the initial call, the recorded statement and the follow-up with the representative, and the details have not shifted.

Entry 8: Nothing independent confirms how the collision happened, so the file remains open pending the provider note and a review of the damage estimate against the impact pattern.
